chunks: As for the report of Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man who is returning from his journey while the time of salat (prayer) has entered and he is still on the road. He said: "He prays two rakʿahs, and if he departs for his journey while the time of salat (prayer) has already entered, then let him pray four."

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four rakʿahs; the complete form of the prayer
key_terms.الطَّرِيقِ: the road; meaning the person is still in transit
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rakʿahs; the shortened travel prayer
key_terms.سَفَرِهِ: his journey; travel that affects the ruling of prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the prescribed time or onset of the prayer period

ai.seo_question: If the time of prayer enters while someone is leaving for or returning from a journey, should he pray two rakʿahs or four?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about salat (prayer) at the boundary between residence and travel. It distinguishes between one returning from travel and one departing for travel after the prayer time has begun, indicating different prayer lengths based on that state.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1288 - Regarding the report of Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:

"I asked him about a man who returns from his journey while the time for prayer has entered, and he is still on the road."
Imam (as) said: "He should pray two rak'ahs (units of prayer). If he sets out on a journey and the time for prayer has already entered, then he should pray four rak'ahs."
